create.title: Exact Li--Yang single-wave phase, carrier, and parameter dictionary
create.statement_tex: For one top-shell reciprocal ray wave, after a finite numerator-sign split, h=a, m=b, H=L, M=D, T=c/kappa_i, and F(z)=1/z give the exact phase ca/(kappa_i b), while F', F'', F''', and F'F'''-3(F'')^2 satisfy the two Li--Yang phase conditions uniformly. The M1 denominator quarter carriers cost O(1), by b=4u+r and F_r(z)=1/(4z+r/M') on four progressions; the M2 chi_4(a) carrier costs O(1), by its two Fourier branches and constant shifts of F. At T asymp Y, H=Y^(1/6), M=Y^(1/2), the repaired Case-A and restricted small-cap hypotheses hold, N_A=Y^(67/300+o(1)), R=Y^(83/600+o(1)), eta=Y^(-17/150+o(1)), and at Q=R the source spacing lengths are Y^(17/600+o(1)) and Y^(17/200+o(1)). The optimized q is (250+10sqrt(170))/91 and Phi(-1/3)=(29+5sqrt(170))/300. This is a dictionary for one already-separated BV source wave only; it does not assert that the literal project ray or pair coefficient satisfies the source coefficient hypotheses.
create.next_action: Use only for individually separated full-scale source waves. Any project estimate must additionally preserve the moving determinant wedge, literal coefficient owners, short-interval transformations, and final absolute-value placement.

create.title: Direct Li--Yang/Bombieri--Iwaniec pair-interface obstruction
create.statement_tex: The repaired Li--Yang standard-sum theorem and its displayed double-large-sieve/two-spacing interface do not directly give a complete exponent below Y^(27/48) for the literal top-shell determinant scalar. The physical pair coefficient remains joint through the one-sided moving determinant wedge, taper, primitive lifts, Mobius/Stieltjes profiles, thresholds, quarter or chi_4 carriers, aliases, stars, cells, signs, and owners; no owner-preserving projective decomposition with a favorable source norm is proved. The source takes arcwise absolute values and returns positive spacing quantities, not a reverse signed operator inequality. Project rays map to original source summation variables, not to the later derivative approximants, and the determinant does not supply the four modular-inverse and real second-spacing conditions. Even granting a rank-one connector, projection, taper, and every owner at zero cost, two independent normalized source bounds give only Y^(2Phi(-1/3)+epsilon)=Y^(0.6279468270...+epsilon)=Y^(30.1414.../48+epsilon), above 27/48. The formal one-source collapse h=n, m=bb' has product-fibre coefficients and violates the source large-M Case-A range. This is a no-go for the audited direct and factor-first source interfaces, not for a new joint determinant-adapted double-large-sieve theorem.
create.next_action: Park the direct and factor-first Li--Yang imports. Reopen this lane only with a new joint theorem that retains the actual pair coefficient before arcwise absolute values, resolves the source first-coordinate seam, maps all four spacings, and proves complete capacity below Y^(27/48).

update.statement_tex: The final real-X inclusive Li--Yang circle theorem is source-audited and independently repaired. The accepted narrow route uses M<T^(7/16), H=MT^x, sqrt(-1-8x) in (5.27), the Bourgain--Watt v1 (7.2) two-sign identity, and a fifth repair: printed Li--Yang (4.9) is not the substitution of Lemma 4.1 condition (4.6) and the Case-A N in (4.8), so corrected (5.23) is used to verify original (4.6) directly. The general printed Proposition 3.1 omits beta_2>=0, the general Case-B comparison omits a logarithm, and general Theorem 4.2 is not certified with (4.9) as printed. On the exact final range, the missing beta_2 condition, Case-B logarithm, and original Lemma condition have explicit fixed-power margins, yielding theta_LY=(3292+25sqrt(1717))/13762. The v2 first-spacing presentation also has an l-versus-k first-coordinate mismatch that must be resolved before a new direct DLS application. The paper remains a preprint and no public erratum was found.
update.reason_for_promotion: Round 133 independently identifies and repairs the false (4.9) substitution on the final narrow range by connecting (5.23) directly to original (4.6), while preserving all Round-95 scope restrictions.
update.next_action: Treat only the narrow five-repair theorem as an external dependency. Do not cite printed (4.9), general Theorem 4.2, the full printed Proposition 3.1, or either unverified first-spacing four-vector as a new project interface.

update.statement_tex: For every epsilon>0 and every real X>=2, the inclusive Gauss-circle discrepancy P(X)=N(sqrt(X))-pi X satisfies P(X)<<_epsilon X^(theta_LY+epsilon), where theta_LY=(3292+25sqrt(1717))/13762=0.3144831759740614.... This accepts only the final application after five literal/source-condition repairs: M<T^(7/16), H=MT^x, sqrt(-1-8x) in Li--Yang (5.27), the exact two-sign circle identity from Bourgain--Watt v1 (7.2), and the direct verification of Lemma 4.1 (4.6) by corrected (5.23) while bypassing false printed (4.9). The missing Guth--Maldague beta_2>=0 condition is proved on the final x-range, and the missing Case-B logarithm is absorbed by fixed-power slack. The printed general Proposition 3.1, general Case-B theorem, and general Theorem 4.2 with (4.9) are not accepted. This direct external theorem does not prove the project's internal cluster theorem, M9-M1, M9-M2, M9, or exponent one quarter.
update.next_action: Use this unchanged numerical exponent as the strongest certified global pointwise benchmark, with all five repairs and nonimplication scope explicit.

The best complete bound remains Y^(35/48). The direct Demeter--Wu and direct or factor-first Li--Yang/BI interfaces are parked. Continue only with a genuinely new joint signed theorem that retains the literal coefficient before positive norms and has a complete capacity below Y^(27/48), or rotate to a distinct accepted proof frontier.

Do not replace the literal signed scalar by a positive source arc sum, first-spacing norm, second-spacing count, SVD, row energy, or two independent source-wave product without a proved one-sided owner-preserving connector and complete norm ledger.
Retain Y^(35/48+epsilon) as the complete top-shell bound. The audited Li--Yang/BI interface gives an exact one-wave dictionary but no complete pair estimate below Y^(27/48).

reject.reason: Direct substitution differs from printed (4.9); after a common power comparison the discrepancy is T^2/M^6, and the two conditions have opposite outcomes at M=T^(1/2), H=T^(1/6).
The final narrow route bypasses false (4.9), but general Theorem 4.2 is not repaired over its whole printed range.
Project rays are original source summation variables with ratio Y^(-1/3) and denominator Y^(1/2); source approximants are created later, have ratio of order one, and denominator at most Y^(1/6).
One ordinary-ratio determinant condition supplies neither modular-inverse coordinate nor the derived floor, mu, and fractional-part coordinates.
The source theorem starts with one separably BV-weighted wave; the project target is an owner-dependent joint pair coefficient with a moving determinant wedge.
No owner-preserving projective decomposition through the source short-interval and major/minor-arc transformations has been proved.
The source takes arcwise absolute values and returns positive spacing quantities; it supplies no reverse signed operator inequality for the project scalar.
Four denominator progressions make the quarter carrier constant and preserve uniform source phase conditions, so the carrier costs O(1); the remaining joint owners are the actual obstruction.
The exact G_q norm and introduction use l as the first coordinate, while the Section-4 sketch prints k; the v2 source does not reconcile them.
The printed exponent is singular at q=4; the endpoint uses the source's separate G_4 estimate.
Even with zero connector cost, the exact exponent is 2Phi(-1/3)=0.6279468270..., which is 30.1414.../48 and exceeds 27/48.
The calculation concerns a factor-first use of two independent one-wave theorems; a genuinely new joint determinant-adapted DLS theorem is a different interface.
Fixed-BV weights can localize short subintervals; the obstruction is the moving nonproduct wedge and absent norm, not short support by itself.
The h=n, m=bb' collapse has a product-fibre coefficient and M asymp T, H asymp T^(9/16), contradicting the large-M Case-A lower condition H at least T^5.
The packet is a per-ray hostile phase control and upper-capacity ledger; one centre does not align every denominator and actual amplitudes may cancel or vanish.
No complete literal pair estimate was proved, so neither the internal one-third theorem nor any M9 or bridge dependency changes.

No uniform all-owner endpoint estimate is proved.
M9-M1, M9-M2, and endpoint uniformity remain open.

The quarter target still lacks M9-M1, M9-M2, endpoint uniformity, M9, and the final unconditional bridge.
